Emma (Head of Product): quick follow-up from today's all-hands Q&A 1 — wanted to capture the concrete asks from customers and what leadership can action. i'll drop the summary here and open for quick clarifying q's.
Raj (Sales): high-level: wins = reliability + simple onboarding; losses = compliance gaps, unpredictable latency, and surprise accuracy regressions after model updates.
Sophia (CS): example loss: FinAssist required FIPS-compliant key storage and we couldn't provide a customer-managed HSM option quickly. they moved to a vendor with on-prem key control.
David (CEO): thanks. which of these are quick fixes vs. multi-sprint investments?
Lin (Eng PM): quick fixes: 1) publish an explicit "VPC quickstart" doc + terraform module (2-3 sprints if we dedicate an eng pair), 2) standardize a fallback model policy that sales can promise. multi-sprint: HSM/KMS enterprise integrations, SLA-grade dedicated capacity.
Maria (Applied ML): on accuracy regressions 1 most were triggered after we changed a default quantization profile for a model family. mitigation: add fingerprinting tests on model onboarding and run a sampled eval on deploys. low-effort: bake a small release-check script into our CI.
Ben (Customer Success): customers consistently ask for: short private deploy path, explicit latency tiers with pricing, an eval kit to reproduce failures, and a clear support escalation for production regressions.
Raj (Sales): prospect request: auto-fallback when dedicated capacity saturates (e.g., route to hosted smaller model with notification & cap). prevents request failures and big billing surprises.
Emma (Head of Product): leadership ask: can we commit to a beta VPC quickstart by end of Q2? this was flagged as deal-blocking by 3 prospects.
David (CEO): provisional yes. need scope & risks from eng + security. can we get a one-pager and a proposed delivery timeline by next Tues?
Lin (Eng PM): will prepare a one-pager. proposed minimal scope: terraform module, sample KMS integration, runbook for 5 common network errors, onboarding checklist. dev estimate: 6 sprint-weeks.
Sophia (CS): also please include a short FAQ on accuracy vs quantization in the one-pager. customers get surprised when small changes change hallucination rates.
Maria (Applied ML): i'll produce a 1-page with examples and recommended quantization profiles per model tier. will include a short test harness.
Ben (Customer Success): i'll compile verbatim customer asks and the exact language they used; that'll help legal & sales craft contractual wording for SLAs.
Raj (Sales): Q for leadership: any appetite to fast-track a "latency premium" product tier where we guarantee p95 with financial credits on misses?
David (CEO): yes, seems feasible. finance + pricing to model costs. offer idea: standard vs premium latency tiers with defined fallback behaviors.
Emma (Head of Product): action items i'm capturing: 1) VPC quickstart one-pager (Lin) 2) quantization FAQ (Maria) 3) loss-playbook draft mapping losses -> mitigations (Ben, Raj, Lin) 4) SLA tier proposal (Finance + Product) 5) eval/regression harness in CI (Maria + Eng).
allhands-bot: :spiral_calendar: created task: "VPC quickstart one-pager" owner: Lin, due: 7 days.
David (CEO): leadership will review the one-pager + proposed commitments at next week's leadership review. please keep items concise and include risks/mitigations.
Sophia (CS): small operational request: if we document recommended batching/quantization tradeoffs, can we include example cost delta numbers? customers ask for concrete tradeoff data.
Maria (Applied ML): yes 1 i'll include sample token cost deltas for common configs.
Lin (Eng PM): i'll add a short note in the one-pager about what "beta" entails (limited customers, support SLA, telemetry hooks) so sales knows what to promise.
Ben (Customer Success): i'll schedule a customer panel with two prospects who pushed back on quickstart to validate the beta scope.
Emma (Head of Product): thanks everyone. follow-up: i'll post the deck and the raw Q&A notes here: https://redwoodhq.internal/allhands/1932009876-notes and will tag owners for tickets. please keep further thread replies brief so i can turn them into tickets.
Raj (Sales): noted, thanks.
David (CEO): appreciate the fast alignment.
Emma (Head of Product): end.
